name: "If it's a X, it …" riders — conditional on what the target is
notes: Found by tests/sweep.py. A second sentence that applies only if the object just named is something (Wedding Invitation "If it's a Vampire, it also gains lifelink", Katsumasa "If it's not a Vehicle, it has base power and toughness 1/1", Tune Up, The Flood of Mars, Lim-Dûl, Rapid Fire "If it doesn't have rampage, that creature gains rampage 2", Tenza "As long as it's red, it has trample") produced nothing. _splitConditionalBranches (cards-text-utils.js) now gives each rider its own line and condition, with the target of the sentence before as its subject and the same target slot; in a fired ability _resolveRiderSubjectToTarget (cards-helpers.js) names that target first so the generic "it → target <trigger subject>" rewrite stays off it. Spell and ability riders are checked once ("on resolution", read from the fire-time snapshot when there is one). Each rider is shown here on a target it applies to and one it does not. A rider whose target has not been picked yet (the third Katsumasa activation, Donatello) must not fall back on the ability's source: the base-P/T and add-type parsers now give a rider's effect its target's restriction, without which a fired ability pins the effect to its source. A later-sentence "if" on a triggered or activated line also no longer hides the whole ability line from the permanent (Wedding Invitation, The Flood of Mars, Hidden Blade).
